title: Project/components names
body:
The discussion has been started on Slack already, but I'd like to continue here. The main issue was that "DroneCore" is close to "Dronecode" which makes it confusing for people. 

I've read propositions of going for "Dronecode Mobile API" and "Dronecode Onboard API".

Feel free to share your opinion here.

comments.body:
### API vs SDK

In my opinion, we should consider what people already know:

* I believe the main one is DJI: DJI Mobile SDK/DJI Onboard SDK (the former being for Android/iOS and the latter in C++)
* The Parrot SDK (on their dev page they call it "the SDK")
* DroneKit. From the official page: "DroneKit offers an SDK and web API".

So I would use "SDK" instead of "API", just because we answer the same problem as these other SDKs.

### Mobile / Onboard

Now, our structure is a bit different than DJI's in that we don't have a concept of "Mobile" vs "Onboard". We could certainly run everything onboard, or everything on the ground, be it on a mobile or not. Of course, not all combinations make sense. But it can be done.

### My proposition

Here is how I personally see DroneCore:
* __Core libraries:__ those are the C++ libraries composed of "core", which does the mavlink communication and maintains the connection to the drone, and the plugins that add features (e.g. `action`, `telemetry`, `mission`).
* __Backend:__ this is a gRPC server wrapping the core libraries and providing a gRPC interface in the form of proto files. The backend may or may not run onboard the drone.
* __Frontends:__ those are language wrappers making a nice interface to the gRPC backend. So as an app developer, instead of having to build my mobile app on top of the proto files defined by the backend, I can use, say, DroneCore-Java, which takes care of the gRPC communication under the hood.

title: Camera range options not supported
body:
We should support camera settings that are not an enum option but rather a range.

An example for such a param can be found in the camera manager:

https://github.com/Dronecode/camera-manager/blob/eef47667506eb97e6ee7349489b7738a825dae14/samples/def/camera-def-uvc.xml#L57-L59

comments.body: @JonasVautherin we'll have to figure out the proto for this first, I think.
Agreed. Is it already needed for a camera we support?

What would be an easier way? Whatever else I can think of implies adding messages per type, and that ends up giving stuff like `SubscribeIntSettings`, `SubscribeEnumSettings`, ... We cannot do fancy `OneOf` or stuff like that, because in the end we have to be able to translate that to all the languages we support.
`SubscribeRangeSettings`? I see the problem, what do you do with the types.

> SubscribeRangeSettings? I see the problem, what do you do with the types.

Exactly. In Java/Swift, we get a stream of one type. Having a supertype (`Object` or `Any`) is quite similar to having a `String`, in the end.

The camera knows that type it wants for each param, so it can check it and return an error for a wrong argument. Which is probably already the case for, say, a range: if I need an `int` betweeen 0 and 10 and I send 15, the camera will complain (`WRONG_ARGUMENT`?). I don't see a problem with doing that as well if I send "fifteen plz".

Same on the client side, when receiving a value. I don't see it as a big problem if users receive "8" (string) and need to cast it to 8 (int) themselves, given that the camera should never send an invalid value like "eight, I think" (string).

That's not the most beautiful interface ever, but if it contains the information needed to write a dynamic interface on the client side while being auto-generated on the SDK side, I believe it is not too bad.

I would be interested in @byuarus and @douglaswsilva opinions, as they have implemented a client side (not yet for the ranges, obviously).

I'm almost convinced :smile:.

One more thing: I think we also need to be able to specify the interval, so what about:

If `is_range == true`, then `repeated Option options` must contain 2 options with `option_value` set respectively to [min, max] or 3 options with `option_value` set respectively to [min, interval, max].

That would make sense to me :+1:.

Possibly we should also provide the type of the values, in case the client needs that? Let's wait for @byuarus and @douglaswsilva for that, maybe :laughing:.

> Possibly we should also provide the type of the values, in case the client needs that? 

@JonasVautherin Yes, you're right. We need this :) 

> If is_range == true, then repeated Option options must contain 2 options with option_value set respectively to [min, max] or 3 options with option_value set respectively to [min, interval, max].

@julianoes  This will work for us.

Currently, for Sony R10C camera, we receive a json file with all possible settings. For R10C they provide the range as an enum, this will work for us too. I would say that it's preferred way of presenting range settings as it will make less likely that client-side will send some weird values. title: Add MAVSDK to Vcpkg
body:
[Vcpkg](https://github.com/Microsoft/vcpkg) is a package manager for C++ with many interesting features. It is based on CMake, supports multiple architectures, provides update mechanisms and integrates with any user project using CMake as its build manager.

Are there plans to add MAVSDK to Vcpkg? It would provide great benefits to developers using MAVSDK in their projects.

comments.body: That would be a very good idea. I would have to read more about how it all works though. If you can give me pointers or instructions how to proceed that would be helpful.

Thank you for considering this suggestion.

**Vcpkg Overview**

Personally, I have been using Vcpkg for some time as an end user. I find it a very useful C++ package manager, which provides an easy mechanism to search, install and update libraries for any supported architecture. This is especially useful when developing on Windows, since libraries can be automatically downloaded, compiled and installed on a single directory, which can then be targeted with CMake rules.

In summary, Vcpkg downloads the library's source code from a public URL (e.g., GitHub repo), compiles the code for the chosen architecture, and installs the library on the predefined Vcpkg directory containing all installed libraries.

Then, developers who want to use these libraries in their projects only need to add Vcpkg's CMake toolchain by appending the following flag to CMake:
"-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=C:/vcpkg/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake"

**Contribute MAVSDK to Vcpkg**

Vcpkg's GitHub page contains instructions on how to add a new library to Vcpkg.
* https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#new-package-guidelines
* https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/tree/master/docs

Essentially, the project maintainer has to submit a PR on Vcpkg with the files required by Vcpkg. I have never submitted a project to Vcpkg, but from my understanding Vcpkg needs two mandatory files and optional patches.

The mandatory files are:
1. ```"CONTROL"```: with the library's informatio
...[truncated]

I skimmed through Vckpg docs and it seems to be well documented.
https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/tree/master/docs

**Dependencies**

According to this [page](https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/blob/master/docs/maintainers/control-files.md), the dependencies of a given project should be listed in the ```CONTROL``` file, which has a syntax based on Debian's Control format. For instance, the curl library in Vcpkg depends on zlib. Thus, the curl's CONTROL file has the following line: ```Build-Depends: zlib```.

Regarding the dependencies of MAVSDK-C++, they are all supported in Vcpkg:

* ```jsoncpp```: https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/tree/master/ports/jsoncpp
* ```tinyxml2```: https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/tree/master/ports/tinyxml2
* ```zlib```: https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/tree/master/ports/zlib
* ```curl```: https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/tree/master/ports/curl

**Portfile**

The instructions for building and installing MAVSDK should be declared in the ```portfile.cmake```.
Vcpkg provides CMake functions to manage this process, which are documented here:
https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/blob/master/docs/maintainers/portfile-functions.md

This page contains an example of packaging a project hosted on GitHub:
https://github.com/microsoft/vcpkg/blob/master/docs/examples/packaging-github-repos.md

Awesome! I think you should try to go for it, then :slightly_smiling_face:. I would personally try to use Vcpkg to build MAVSDK first (as opposed to writing the portfile to make a package out of MAVSDK):

1. Clone MAVSDK
2. Setup your Vcpkg to get the dependencies (`jsoncpp`, `tinyxml2`, `zlib`, `curl`)
3. Build MAVDSK with the toolchain, as per your instructions above (don't forget to disable the superbuild). So something like:

```cmake
cmake -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=C:/vcpkg/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake -DSUPERBUILD=OFF -Bbuild -S.
cmake --build build
```

If this builds, it means that MAVSDK was built using the dependencies from Vcpkg. Next step would then be to write the portfile to make a package out of MAVSDK, I guess.

On the other hand, it seems Microsoft is designing a new declarative method (using manifests) for Vcpkg, in order for users to specify the libraries used in their projects in a source-controlled file, as well as for maintainers to publish their own libraries. The draft is available on Vcpkg's GitHub:

comments.body: I think that this is more a question for PX4. The autopilot is the one "executing" the mission and actually triggering the camera in that case :+1:.

It's a bit confusing because there is the MAVSDK Action TAKE_PHOTO which sends the command [MAV_CMD_IMAGE_START_CAPTURE](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_IMAGE_START_CAPTURE) in PX4 to a potential camera.

However, this doesn't actually set up triggering on PX4. To use triggering, you have to set up the trigger pin in the Actuator setting, and then use MissionRaw and use the command [MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST), or [MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_INTERVAL](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_INTERVAL)
@JonasVautherin @julianoes This is probably a PX4 question too, but there is no "Actuators" menu in my QGC, is that because I selected the wrong or an incompatible airframe?

> @JonasVautherin @julianoes This is probably a PX4 question too, but there is no "Actuators" menu in my QGC, is that because I selected the wrong or an incompatible airframe?

I could solve this just going to the airframe file in /init.d/airframes, disable the mixer and enabling the SYS_CTRL_ALLOC, and then setting all the necessary PWM functions up. In my case, i set `param set-default PWM_AUX_FUNC5 2000  # Camera trigger` for the pwm trigger.

After this i could see the Actuators menu in QGC.

Then, to trigger, make sure you set up the parameters for TRIG_PWM_NEUTRAL and TRIG_PWM_SHOOT. also you could set the TRIG_INTERFACE to generic pwm and TRIG_MODE to 1 for example.

To activate the trigger just send a pymavlink command long [MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_CMD_DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST) and wait for ACK

mavlink协议 是通过 ID 进行区分
一个无人机，在系统中是一个 system，通过system id进行区分
同一个无人的多个功能模块例如照相、gps，通过component id进行区分，不管有多少个connection，都将给更新同一个system。

Translation:
The MAVLink protocol distinguishes a single drone by ID. In the system, a drone is considered one "system," identified by a system ID. Multiple functional modules within the same drone — such as the camera and GPS — are distinguished by component ID. Regardless of how many connections there are, they all update the same system. These IDs are all configured in the drone's firmware.
